newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sets stricter rule on forex assets.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sets stricter rule on forex assets.

text.p: Philippine banks would be required to set aside 30 percent of its foreign exchange assets in cash or short-term securities, Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said on Thursday.
At present, banks can place their assets in any form of securities and loans of varying maturities. Banks' foreign exchange liabilities should be fully covered with foreign exchange assets.
The new regulation was approved on Wednesday by the Central Bank's Monetary Board. The implementing guideline is scheduled to be released on Friday.

Reyes said the move is a prudent measure for banks to easily cover their liabilities, especially when there is a huge withdrawal of foreign currency deposits. The new regulation will be effective immediately, he added.
At present, about 50 percent of banks' foreign exchange assets are in long-term loans.
The Philippine banking industry was recently hit by speculation that it may have overextended foreign exchange loans and may suffer the same crisis as Thailand.
